title: Acyclicity of arbitrary modules over smooth functions
statement: Let $N$ be a Hausdorff second-countable smooth real manifold without boundary, locally modeled on finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces; the local dimension may vary between connected components. Then $N$ is paracompact, meaning that every open cover admits a locally finite open refinement. Let $\mathcal E_N$ be the sheaf $U\mapsto C^\infty(U,\mathbf C)$ with pointwise ring operations. For every sheaf $F$ of unital $\mathcal E_N$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], its underlying abelian sheaf $F_{\mathrm{ab}}$ satisfies $H^r(N,F_{\mathrm{ab}})=0$ for every $r>0$. Here $H^r$ is the right derived global-sections functor in abelian sheaves on the site of open subsets of $N$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. No local freeness, coherence, or finite-rank condition on $F$ is assumed.

source.place: WANTED locally; read online https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/agbook.pdf. IV §4, discussion following Definition (4.4), printed p.203 (locally compact spaces with countable base are paracompact); Example (4.12), Theorem (4.15), Lemma (4.18), Corollary (4.19), printed pp.204--205. The soft-ring argument applies to the sheaf of complex-valued smooth functions and does not use a uniform dimension bound.

proof.text: Each point has a chart containing the inverse image of a small closed Euclidean ball about its image; this is a compact neighborhood, so $N$ is locally compact. Apply [lem-sfb-locally-compact-countable-paracompact] with the assumed Hausdorff and second-countability hypotheses. Thus $N$ is $\sigma$-compact, paracompact and normal. This proves the topological clause.

source.place: IV §4.B, printed p.203; locally compact countable-base case supplied by the cited Mathlib leaf.

proof.text: Fix disjoint closed subsets $A,B\subseteq N$. The connected components $C$ of $N$ are open: a sufficiently small coordinate ball about any point is connected and contained in its component. Each $C$ is a Hausdorff second-countable locally compact manifold of one fixed finite dimension, by the componentwise dimension convention in the statement. The topological leaf gives normality and $\sigma$-compactness of $C$. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-separating-cutoff] to $A\cap C,B\cap C$ on $C$. The functions $u_C$ define $u:N\to\mathbf R$ on the disjoint open components. It is smooth since smoothness is local; unions of the componentwise open neighborhoods show that $u=0$ near $A$ and $u=1$ near $B$. Viewed as a complex-valued function, $u$ is a section of $\mathcal E_N$ (its imaginary part is zero).

source.place: IV §4, Example (4.12) and cutoff in Lemma (4.18), pp.204--205; componentwise assembly of the Mathlib cutoff.

proof.text: Put $G=F_{\mathrm{ab}}$. Let $S\subseteq N$ be closed and $s\in\Gamma(S,G|_S)$. Since $N$ is paracompact Hausdorff, [lem-sfb-closed-section-neighborhood-extension] gives an open $U\supseteq S$ and $t\in G(U)$ restricting to $s$. Apply the preceding cutoff construction with $A=N\setminus U$ and $B=S$. We obtain $u\in\mathcal E_N(N)$ equal to zero on an open neighborhood $W$ of $N\setminus U$, and equal to one on a neighborhood of $S$.

source.place: IV §4, Corollary (4.8), p.204, and proof of Lemma (4.18), p.205.

proof.text: Use the module action to form $(u|_U)t\in F(U)$. On $U\cap W$ this is $0t=0$, so it glues with the zero section of $F(W)$ on the open cover $U\cup W=N$. The sheaf axiom produces $\widetilde s\in F(N)$. Along $S$ the scalar $u$ is one, hence $\widetilde s|_S=1s=s$ by unitality. This proves directly that the abelian sheaf $G$ is soft. Only multiplication by a scalar and sheaf gluing were used; there was no finiteness assumption on $F$.

source.place: IV §4, proof of Lemma (4.18), p.205; open-neighborhood vanishing makes extension by zero a sheaf gluing.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-soft-abelian-sheaf-acyclic] to the paracompact Hausdorff space $N$ and the soft abelian sheaf $G$ just constructed. It gives $R^r\Gamma(N,G)=0$ for every $r>0$, exactly the cohomology convention in the statement. No passage between module-derived and abelian-derived functors is involved.
